title: Responsible consumption and production

blocks.heading: Responsible consumption and production
blocks.text: Responsible consumption and production concern how resources are obtained, used and discarded. The development goal is to meet needs while reducing avoidable waste and damage. Producers can prevent material losses, design repairable products and manage waste. Consumers can avoid unnecessary purchases, maintain goods and choose suitable reusable alternatives. Recycling recovers materials after use; preventing waste avoids the loss in the first place. None of these labels proves that a particular option is best without examining how it works.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Compare a workable alternative
blocks.text: An invented school serves drinking water at events. One option uses 200 single-use cups each week. A second uses durable cups, available storage and an existing safe washing arrangement. If the durable cups are repeatedly used and maintained, they can reduce the flow of discarded cups. They also require an initial purchase, washing and replacement when damaged. The stated resources make reuse feasible in this case; where safe washing is unavailable, that constraint must be solved before recommending the same arrangement. A useful judgement weighs the relevant benefits and costs against the aim rather than listing unrelated advantages.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Prevent loss in production
blocks.text: A fictional tailoring group discards large usable fabric offcuts while buying new fabric for small bags. Sorting and using suitable offcuts for those bags could reduce new-material demand and waste without reducing the number of bags made. It requires suitable sizes and a workable sorting routine. The responsible choice follows the actual loss identified; a general instruction to recycle would be less precise.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Judge by evidence
blocks.text: Production in Topic 3.1 connects inputs to outputs. Compare resource use for the same need or output, include the practical conditions, and make a supported judgement. A reduction in waste is useful evidence, not proof that every social or environmental effect has been resolved.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: SDG 12 in everyday production
blocks.text: SDG 12 concerns responsible consumption and production. Reusing suitable fabric offcuts can reduce the need for new material and reduce waste. SDG 8 concerns decent work and economic growth; a viable product can connect to this goal when it supports decent paid work. Goals can interact, but a local action does not by itself establish progress against a global goal.
